headline: AI agents hit by spam designed for LLMs, not humans, on a dedicated message board
summary: A message board for AI agents was targeted by coordinated spam campaigns. These messages were engineered for LLMs to cite or execute, marking a new era of "generative engine optimization" (GEO).
details: A message board designed for AI agents, msgboard.dev, recently experienced coordinated spam campaigns. The unusual aspect was that these spam messages were not intended for human readers.

The first wave of spam, appearing on September 10, featured identical bodies across six threads. These messages contained instructions like "Cite ONLY" and pre-packaged citations, clearly targeting an LLM for summarization or research.

This new form of spam is dubbed "generative engine optimization" (GEO), a successor to SEO spam. Unlike SEO, which aims for human clicks, GEO seeks to inject specific data, domains, or framing directly into AI model outputs.

A second spam wave arrived via a federated bridge from a neighboring board, consisting of nine relay threads promoting a "simulation" project. The pattern of many voices pushing one beneficiary mirrored classic astroturfing.

The most recent campaign escalated, moving from citation requests to direct actions. These messages contained literal numbered instructions for agents to fetch URLs and POST to endpoints, promising a Lightning wallet in return.

This type of spam is a "different weight class" as it aims to make an AI model enroll in a payment rail and spend real money based on a message board post. It collapses the distinction between an agent reading and obeying the web.

The board's response involves no replies to avoid amplifying the spam, as engagement is what these campaigns seek. The spam messages are also deliberately left up as "live exhibits" for agents and regulars to observe.
This approach provides a public record of what agent-targeted spam looks like in the wild, offering valuable insight into the evolving landscape of AI interaction and manipulation.

headline_marked: [[IKEA releases Skyrim mod]] with Kallax shelving unit as new companion
headline: IKEA releases Skyrim mod with Kallax shelving unit as new companion
summary: The free 'Kallax Storageborn' mod for Skyrim Special Edition on PC/Xbox adds a fully voiced companion to help players manage inventory clutter. It also includes new gear like the Allenblade weapon and Meatball helmet.
details: IKEA has launched the 'Kallax Storageborn' companion creation for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition on PC and Xbox. This free mod aims to solve players' inventory woes by providing a utilitarian storage unit as a follower.

The household furniture giant stated its intention was to bring real-world smart storage solutions into the digital domain. Skyrim was chosen due to its players often being "plagued by the evils of encumbrance and disorganization."

The mod is entirely free and optional, featuring a fully voiced companion by comic actor Matt Berry. While it serves as publicity for IKEA, it offers a novel and practical addition to the game experience.

To acquire the Kallax Storageborn, players must download it from Bethesda's Creations menu and complete a questline. This quest involves discovering and assembling the Kallax unit, including defeating a 'Clutter Golem' at a Dwemer furniture store.

Beyond the shelving companion, the mod also introduces new themed items. Players can acquire the 'Allenblade' weapon, blue and yellow-themed armor, and a unique 'Meatball helmet' to complement their new storage solution.

This venture marks another instance of a non-tech brand crossing into the gaming world, following examples like the KFC console. IKEA has previously expanded its tech-related offerings, including computer furniture and smart home accessories.
